findings.comment: Site plan does not include a note stating that the site lies within the Austin Energy service area, as required for all sites within the AE service area.

Plans do not include the required developer responsibility note stating that the developer is responsible for designing and constructing all conduit and related infrastructure to current Austin Energy Electric Service Standards, including conductor installation costs, and for coordinating with other utilities to resolve conflicts.

applicableAreas: Electrical transformer and pull box locations
findings.comment: Austin Energy approval for electrical transformer and pull box design has not been documented on file. While Austin Energy has completed a preliminary design review and provided redline comments via Bluebeam, final design approval from AE has not been submitted with the site plan or documented as received.

Electrical easement documentation and coordination with Austin Energy have not been verified. Site plan notes indicate 'Additional electric easements may be required at a later date,' but evidence of final layout coordination with AE or recorded easement documents has not been provided with the site plan set.

applicableAreas: Land development application to Austin Energy
findings.comment: Submission of a georeferenced AutoCAD drawing (version 2016 or newer) to Austin Energy with all required content (easements, existing facilities, permanent structures with footprint/height, final topology, property lines, setbacks) for the land development application has not been documented. While preliminary electrical design is shown on Sheet 21, evidence of the full ESPA/AE design application with compliant AutoCAD deliverable has not been provided.

applicableAreas: Transformer pad and pull box locations
findings.comment: Plans do not demonstrate that proposed development will not limit Austin Energy personnel access to existing or proposed electric facilities. Proposed transformer pads and pull boxes are shown on Sheet 21, but no explicit access paths or truck access dimensions (minimum 12-ft width and 16-ft vertical clearance) are provided to ensure AE equipment access.

AULCC coordination status cannot be verified from available documents. While water utility tap work (~72 LF) is shown on Sheet 20, the total linear footage of ROW utility construction/excavation (including wastewater connections and any other ROW work) cannot be confirmed from the site plan set to determine if the 300 LF citywide or 25 LF DAPCZ thresholds are met. No AULCC Completeness Letter is provided with the site plan.

Gattan clearance status cannot be verified. No documentation confirming whether Gattan infrastructure is present in or affected by the project, or whether Gattan clearance has been obtained, is provided with the site plan set.

Telecommunications provider clearances have not been documented. No correspondence or clearance letters from telecommunications providers indicating that project infrastructure does not conflict with telecom facilities is provided with the site plan set.

Dry utility clearances from applicable providers (gas, electric, and other dry utilities) have not been documented. While Austin Energy has completed preliminary review, clearance from other dry utility providers (gas, etc.) for the underground electric line shown along Valley View Road frontage has not been provided.

ROW utility coordination case closure status cannot be verified from the site plan set. The case status in the site plan case management system is not visible in the submitted documents, and no documentation confirming that the ROW utility coordination case has been closed or completed is provided.

Additional Review Acknowledgement table is not present on the cover sheet. All sites require a completed Additional Review Acknowledgement table listing all applicable external reviews and approvals (e.g., TxDOT, railroad, gas company, TCEQ, water districts, easement acquisition, county approval, service extension, etc.) before final site plan approval.

Addressing plan approval has not been documented. While Sheet 29 shows the addressing plan with unit numbering, evidence of approval from 911 Addressing/Address Management Services has not been provided with the site plan set. An Address Validation Letter, if issued, does not constitute an approved addressing plan.

Transmission easement plat notes cannot be fully verified from available documents. While extensive Electric Transmission Notes are present on Sheet 3, confirmation that all eight required AEDC 1.16.0(8) plat notes are present on the plat sheet itself (Sheet 2), including the specific 48-hour notice requirement, has not been verified. Additionally, confirmation that no portion of the transmission easement is labeled as parkland or proposed for parkland dedication per AEDC 1.16.0(9) cannot be confirmed from the submitted documents.
